title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten under-21-safe outings around John Carroll University and greater Cleveland with direct evidence that admission, reservations, or purchases are not required.

cards.title: Walk a Loop at The Walt
cards.subtitle: Perimeter track and green space in University Heights
cards.notes: Meet at the Fenwick Road entrance, walk the perimeter track together, then use the first-come picnic tables or gazebo for a break.
cards.short_summary: A dawn-to-dusk neighborhood loop with gathering spaces, exercise stations, and natural areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists a perimeter walking track, green space, exercise stations, picnic tables, benches, and a gazebo available without reservations at Walter Stinson Community Park.
cards.access_notes: Public city park at 2313 Fenwick Road; open dawn to dusk. Picnic tables and benches are first come, and gazebo reservations are unavailable.

cards.title: Pack a Pavilion Picnic
cards.subtitle: Resident-access picnic stop near Cedar Road
cards.notes: Bring food from home, claim no more than two tables under the shelter, and keep the gathering within the posted two-hour limit.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own picnic hang beneath Purvis Park’s open shelter.
cards.evidence_claim: The city says Purvis Park has sheltered picnic tables and benches, requires no pavilion reservations or permits, and makes tables available first come for up to two hours.
cards.access_notes: University Heights residents only; park hours are dawn to dusk. No pavilion permit or reservation is required. Pool access is separate and excluded.

cards.title: Trade Picks in the Permanent Galleries
cards.subtitle: A free art walk through the main museum
cards.notes: Choose one permanent-gallery work apiece, regroup in the atrium, and explain your picks without adding a ticketed exhibition.
cards.short_summary: A no-ticket-required gallery exchange built around the museum’s permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cleveland Museum of Art states that general admission to its permanent collection galleries is always free; select exhibitions and events may require tickets.
cards.access_notes: Enter the main museum during posted public hours and stay with permanent-collection galleries. Parking and select exhibitions may cost extra.

cards.title: Circle the Ledges Trail
cards.subtitle: A 1.8-mile sandstone loop in Cuyahoga Valley
cards.notes: Start at the trailhead map, follow the signed loop with sturdy shoes, and stay off the fragile rock formations while hiking together.
cards.short_summary: A rocky woodland circuit around the park’s named sandstone formations.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the Ledges Trail as a year-round 1.8-mile loop with no activity fee and no reservation requirement.
cards.access_notes: No activity fee or reservation; Cuyahoga Valley National Park charges no entrance fee. Use daylight hours because the parking lot closes at dusk.

cards.title: Loop Past Brandywine Falls
cards.subtitle: A waterfall-and-footbridge hike in the national park
cards.notes: Arrive early or late to improve parking odds, use the trailhead map, and keep the group on marked paths through the gorge.
cards.short_summary: A 1.5-mile gorge circuit with a waterfall overlook and creek crossing.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Brandywine Gorge Loop as a year-round hike with no activity fee and no reservation requirement.
cards.access_notes: No activity fee or reservation; park entrance is free. The area closes at dusk, parking is limited, and the unpaved loop is not wheelchair accessible.

cards.title: Wildlife-Watch at Beaver Marsh
cards.subtitle: A short Towpath Trail walk from Ira Trailhead
cards.notes: Walk a quarter mile north from Ira Trailhead to the boardwalk, pause at the viewing platforms, and bring binoculars if you have them.
cards.short_summary: An easy out-and-back to wetland viewing platforms along the Towpath Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service recommends the Ira Trailhead-to-Beaver Marsh walk, lists the activity fee as none, and notes picnic, restroom, bench, and tactile-exhibit access.
cards.access_notes: No activity fee; Cuyahoga Valley National Park has no entrance fee. Leashed pets are allowed on the Towpath Trail but not in park buildings.

cards.title: Explore the Park Story Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Self-guided displays inside a restored 1905 store
cards.notes: Begin downstairs with the park overview, continue through the upstairs story exhibits, and collect free trail maps before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced indoor introduction to Cuyahoga Valley’s landscapes and history.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says visitors may explore Boston Mill Visitor Center’s exhibits at their own pace, with no activity fee, reservation, or park entrance charge.
cards.source_title: Stop by Boston Mill Visitor Center
cards.access_notes: Free entry and no reservation. Visit during current visitor-center hours; store merchandise and food are optional purchases and unnecessary for the activity.

cards.title: Work Through the Canal Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Hands-on Ohio & Erie Canal history
cards.notes: Allow at least 30 minutes for the exhibits, compare favorite canal details, and use the trailhead kiosk for an optional Towpath walk.
cards.short_summary: An accessible, hands-on history session inside a former canal-side tavern.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service describes the Canal Exploration Center as a hands-on exhibit visit lasting 30–120 minutes with no activity fee or reservation.
cards.access_notes: No activity fee or reservation; the national park has no entrance fee. Check seasonal operating hours before leaving. The building is wheelchair accessible.

cards.title: Ride the East Rim Loops
cards.subtitle: Intermediate single-track riding near Boston Mills Road
cards.notes: Bring your own bike and helmet, check the posted daily trail status, then follow the day’s one-way direction through an appropriate loop.
cards.short_summary: A fee-free group ride across four named, intermediate trail segments.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists East Rim mountain biking as having no activity fee or reservation and identifies four trails for intermediate riders.
cards.source_title: Go Mountain Biking in Cuyahoga Valley
cards.access_notes: No fee or reservation when using your own bike; park entry is free. Trails may close in wet or icy conditions, so check current status first.

cards.entity_name: Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Market at Howe Meadow
cards.title: Browse the Howe Meadow Market
cards.subtitle: A purchase-optional seasonal market outing
cards.notes: Walk the vendor rows together, compare seasonal displays, and enjoy the market atmosphere without treating a purchase as part of the plan.
cards.short_summary: A free-entry browse through a seasonal national-park farmers market.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service explicitly states there is no fee to attend Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Markets and that money is needed only if a visitor chooses to purchase something.
cards.source_title: Visit Cuyahoga Valley Farms and Markets
cards.access_notes: Attendance requires no fee or reservation, and purchases are optional. Confirm the current market calendar and location before traveling.
